headline: EvoPathBench tests whether self-evolving agents retain and adapt capabilities
summary: A September 21 preprint introduces EvoPathBench, an author-built benchmark for tracking persistent agent memory and skill updates across 1,800 ordered task streams. It tests held-out generalization, retention after unrelated learning and adaptation after a rule changes. In the reported experiments, gains often weakened under distribution shift, retention loss was concentrated in some paths, and no method showed reliable rule adaptation; adaptation effects were not statistically significant after Holm correction. The paper also reports that update-selection safeguards reduce harmful accepted changes but miss more beneficial ones. These results come from fixed configurations in constructed trading environments combining public Binance data and calibrated synthetic trajectories. They are not independently reproduced and do not establish deployed-agent or real-market performance.
